title: David Chanoff
source:
{{Short description|American author}}

'''David Chanoff''' (born November 15, 1943, in [[Philadelphia]]) is an American author of non-fiction work. His work has typically involved collaborations with the principal protagonist of the work concerned. His collaborators have included [[Augustus A. White]], [[Joycelyn Elders]], [[Doan Van Toai|Đoàn Văn Toại]], [[William J. Crowe]], [[Ariel Sharon]], [[Kenneth Good (anthropologist)|Kenneth Good]] and [[Felix Zandman]], among others. He has also written about a wide range of subjects including literary history, education and foreign for ''[[The Washington Post]]'', ''[[The New Republic]]'' and ''[[The New York Times Magazine]]''.

Chanoff founded [[Sudbury Valley School]] in [[Framingham, Massachusetts]] in 1968. In the late 1970s and early 1980s, he taught English at [[Tufts University]] and [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Chanoff, David 1943- |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/educational-magazines/chanoff-david-1943 |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=[[Encyclopedia.com]] |archive-date=2023-06-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604220432/https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/educational-magazines/chanoff-david-1943 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2015, Chanoff's ''Breaking Ground: My Life in Medicine'', co-written with  [[Louis W. Sullivan]], won the [[NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Literary Work – Biography/Autobiography]].<ref name="2015 Image Award Winners">{{cite web |last=Washington |first=Arlene |date=February 6, 2015 |title=2015 Image Winners |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/naacp-image-awards-2015-winners-771018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160427142348/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/naacp-image-awards-2015-winners-771018 |archive-date=April 27, 2016 |accessdate=May 10, 2016 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Chanoff was born November 15, 1943, in Philadelphia to William and Golda ({{Nee|Levin}}) Chanoff. He received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] from [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1965, after which he attended [[Brandeis University]], where he earned a [[Master of Arts]] in 1967 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1973.<ref name=":0" />

On February 18, 1968, Chanoff married Liisa Laikari. He has three children.<ref name=":0" />

Chanoff is ethnically Jewish.<ref name=":0" />
